clue.text: Group union turned on Guardian writer

indicators.note: on here means the following pieces are placed after the first piece

parts.note: a guardian angel watches over someone
a lot is a batch or group of things

indicators.note: turned means this short word is flipped round to run the other way

parts.note: 'it' is slang for sex, a sexual union

explanation.surface: A group's labour union turns its support to a writer for the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but gives ANGEL; 'turned' makes TI from IT. Marion Polk Angellotti was an American writer of pulp fiction and novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Marion Polk Angellotti was an American novelist and short-story author, so she is a writer.

clue.text: A car manufacturer sheds American gang leader

indicators.note: sheds means the car maker's name loses these letters, cast off like a skin

parts.note: Lexus is the Japanese luxury car maker

explanation.surface: A carmaker drops its American gangland boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds' takes US from LEXUS, leaving LEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex leads his band of droogs in Anthony Burgess's A Clockwork Orange, so he is a literary gang boss.

clue.text: Prisoner set up by tense producer of The Annals of the Parish

definitions.text: producer of The Annals of the Parish

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means this word is lifted so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lag is slang for a convict
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An inmate is framed by a nervous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns LAG into GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galt, the Scottish novelist, wrote The Annals of the Parish (1821), so he is its author.

clue.text: Will a role with RSC put out maths lecturer?

indicators.note: put out means these letters are disturbed and set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the Royal Shakespeare Company

explanation.surface: Would an actor's part with the Royal Shakespeare Company upset a mathematics don?
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' shuffles WILLAROLERSC. The RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Alice was Charles Dodgson, mathematics tutor at Christ Church, Oxford, and Lewis Carroll was his pen name.

clue.text: Hard worker has no time for Nick Chopper, perhaps

definitions.note: describes something kept for the Tin Woodman, whose real name is Nick Chopper

indicators.note: has no time means the word loses the letter standing for time

parts.note: a toiler is someone who works hard

explanation.surface: A grafter has no time for a character from Oz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no time' removes T from TOILER. Nick Chopper is the Tin Woodman of Oz, who rusts and needs regular oiling, so an oil can is what is kept for him.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is an oil can, the tool the rusting tin man of Oz needs at hand to keep his joints moving.

clue.text: Third-born criminal gets doomed McCullough singer

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters are crooked and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A third child turned crook takes on an ill-fated songbird from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges THIRDBORN. Colleen McCullough's The Thorn Birds takes its title from a legendary bird that sings once, impaling itself on a thorn.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend behind McCullough's novel, this bird sings its one perfect song while dying on a thorn.

clue.text: Hoods knocking off top in Hermes etc.

definitions.note: plural: Hermes and others like it

indicators.note: knocking off top means the first letter of this word is struck away

parts.note: cowls are monks' hoods

explanation.surface: Hooded figures are toppled among the Greek gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking off top' takes C from COWLS. Hermes is not the god here but Percy Weasley's owl in the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes is the pet bird of Percy Weasley in Harry Potter, one of the novels' messenger birds of prey.

clue.text: In which Dylar is found in iodine-infused wine bouquet

parts.note: white is a kind of wine

indicators.note: infused means this element is steeped into the middle of the following word

parts.note: a wine's nose is its bouquet or aroma
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A drug is detected in the bouquet of a wine laced with iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infused' puts I inside NOSE to give NOISE. Dylar is the experimental drug in Don DeLillo's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Don DeLillo's 1985 novel centres on Dylar, a pill meant to cure the fear of death.

clue.text: Scruffy tramp's entertained by polished Apple product

indicators.note: entertained by means the following letters are taken into this word like a guest

parts.note: shone can mean polished, as in shone his shoes

indicators.note: scruffy suggests the letters are untidy and need sorting

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An unkempt vagrant is hosted by a smart owner of an iPhone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruffy' signals the anagram of the vagrant and 'entertained by' the container; 'polished' is a past tense verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple makes the iPhone, a mobile handset with computing power.

clue.text: She did lines with everyone in story about helmsman

indicators.note: about means the story with its contents is turned to run backwards
in means these letters sit inside the word for story

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
all means everyone
a cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A woman read her lines with the whole cast in a tale about a steersman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts WALL inside LIE to give LIWALLE, and 'about' reverses that to ELLAWIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Wheeler Wilcox was an American poet, so she wrote lines of verse.

clue.text: Help with article on musical work

parts.note: aid means help
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Assistance with a newspaper piece on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Aida is an opera, a large-scale piece for the stage set to music.

clue.text: Engineer messing around with rota for WWl work

indicators.note: messing around with means these letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A mechanic tinkers with the duty schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing around with' signals the anagram of both words. Pat Barker's novel is set at Craiglockhart, a First World War military hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Barker's 1991 novel about Siegfried Sassoon at Craiglockhart is a First World War novel.

clue.text: "They could never become acquainted. It was a perpetual —" (Austen)

definitions.text: "They could never become acquainted. It was a perpetual —" (Austen)

parts.words: "They could never become acquainted. It was a perpetual —" (Austen)
parts.note: a quotation from Jane Austen's Persuasion with its last word missing: the word for a lasting state of being apart

explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Persuasion, describing Anne Elliot's former bond with Captain Wentworth.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names a lasting state of separation and coolness between two people who were once close.

clue.text: Perec's novel description of Rip Van Winkle?

definitions.meaning: Georges Perec's Un homme qui dort, in English translation
Rip Van Winkle slept for twenty years, so he could be described this way

explanation.definitionFit: Perec's 1967 novel is known in English by this title, and Washington Irving's Rip Van Winkle is a man who slept for twenty years.

clue.text: Unstable man hunts UK Nobel prize winner

indicators.note: unstable means the letters are wobbly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unbalanced man hunts down a British prizewinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unstable' shuffles MANHUNTSUK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian novelist of Hunger won the 1920 Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: In-country soldier knocked back hot gigolo

indicators.note: in placed before the country means the soldier sits inside it

parts.note: Mali is a West African country
a soldier ant is a worker of the ant colony

indicators.note: knocked back means this word is turned to read in reverse

parts.note: in means fashionable or hot

explanation.surface: A soldier at home, turned back, sets up as a lover for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container and 'knocked back' the reversal. Mr Mantalini is the idle, philandering husband of a milliner in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Mr Mantalini lives off his wife's money and flirts with other women, a kept man.

clue.text: "The fear of appearances is the first symptom of —" (Dostoevsky)

definitions.text: "The fear of appearances is the first symptom of —" (Dostoevsky)

parts.words: "The fear of appearances is the first symptom of —" (Dostoevsky)
parts.note: a quotation from Dostoevsky with its last word missing: the word for powerlessness

explanation.walkthrough: The line is attributed to Dostoevsky; the missing word means a lack of power or strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names powerlessness, the weakness that fear of how things look reveals.

clue.text: Age of Innocence's last chapter enthrals half-cut Pope

indicators.note: enthrals means these letters hold the following ones captive inside them
last points to the final letter of the novel's name
half-cut means only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: The final chapter of a Wharton novel has a drunken pontiff in its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Age of Innocence' reads as Wharton's title but splits: 'Age' is the definition. 'last' takes the final E, 'half-cut' (British slang for drunk) halves Pope, and 'enthrals' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era or period of history.

clue.text: Books penned by short geek and marginal writer

indicators.note: penned by means the books are enclosed within the other word as in a pen
short means the word is cut and loses its final letter

parts.note: a nerd is a geek
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Volumes written by a clipped bookworm and a writer in the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts NERD to NER, and 'penned by' puts OT inside it. 'Books' as OT (Old Testament) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A noter is someone who makes notes, the kind of reader who writes in a book's margins.

clue.text: Possibly Jack Belicec's small school for every child

parts.note: a pod is a small school of whales or dolphins
per means for every
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Perhaps a fictional character goes to a little school for each pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Belicec is a character in Jack Finney's The Body Snatchers who is replaced by an alien duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Body Snatchers, people are replaced by alien duplicates grown in seed pods.

clue.text: Babalon is funny: a master clown

indicators.note: funny means the letters behave oddly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A city in decline is comic: a fine clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' shuffles AMASTERCLOWN. Babalon is the goddess of Aleister Crowley's Thelema, styled after the woman of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowley's Babalon is the Whore of Babylon from Revelation, an adulterous figure in red.

clue.text: Hunter Thompson's penultimate hit Republican sent up

indicators.note: penultimate picks out the letter just before the last of the name
sent up in a down clue means these letters are pushed to read upwards

parts.note: a number one, written NO 1, is a chart-topping hit

explanation.surface: Gonzo writer Hunter S. Thompson's late success is mocked by a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penultimate' gives O from Thompson; 'sent up' turns NO1 + R into R1ON, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the giant hunter of Greek myth, now a constellation.

clue.text: Jot down only the third husband with sex appeal

indicators.note: only the third means just the third letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Note down just the third husband with charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jot down' looks like the instruction to write; 'only the third' takes W from down.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in not a whit, like a jot or iota.

clue.text: God is mostly peculiar, I ultimately complain

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: odd means peculiar

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: God is a bit strange, I finally grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ODD to OD; 'ultimately' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Language in poetry head of VQR censored

indicators.note: censored means that letter is cut out of the word for poetry

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the journal's initials

explanation.surface: Words in a poem have the editor of a quarterly review censoring them.
explanation.walkthrough: VQR is the Virginia Quarterly Review; 'head of' gives V, which 'censored' takes out of VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Awfully fine Hindus like Shekhar: Ek Jivani

indicators.note: awfully means the letters are in a dreadful mess and need sorting

explanation.surface: Fine Hindus are said to be fond of a Hindi novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' shuffles FINEHINDUS. Agyeya's Hindi novel Shekhar: Ek Jivani appeared in two volumes; its planned third never came.
explanation.definitionFit: Agyeya never completed the third volume of his novel, leaving it incomplete.

clue.text: Gabilan is one at work in Paisley's outskirts

indicators.note: in means these letters sit inside the town's outer letters
outskirts picks the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A man at work on the edge of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts' gives P and Y from Paisley, a town near Glasgow. Gabilan is the colt in John Steinbeck's The Red Pony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabilan is the red colt given to the boy Jody in Steinbeck's The Red Pony.

clue.text: Tartt's alma mater is sadly not benign, knight admitted

indicators.note: admitted means this letter is let in among the others
sadly means the letters are in a sorry state and must be rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Sadly, a writer's old college is far from kind and has let in a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' shuffles NOTBENIGN, and 'admitted' puts N among the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna Tartt studied at Bennington College in Vermont, the model for the college of The Secret History.
